standard_prerequisites.name: Accessibility
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a binary relation on a set, the accessible elements form an inductive family: an element is accessible when every element below it is accessible.
standard_prerequisites.use: Well-foundedness is defined as accessibility of every element, and the first direction of the proof is an induction on an accessibility witness.

standard_prerequisites.name: Propositional truncation and mere existence
standard_prerequisites.statement: A type is merely inhabited when its propositional truncation has an element, and a mere proposition is inhabited exactly when it is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement speaks of subsets that merely have a minimal element, and the second direction argues through truncation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Excluded middle
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every mere proposition the disjunction of it and its negation holds.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis of the counted lemma in both directions; it is used at the end of the second direction to turn mere accessibility into accessibility.

core_obligations: Assume the relation is well-founded, assume a subset B with no minimal element, so that for every a in B there merely exists b below a with b in B, and prove by induction on an accessibility witness that no element lies in B (source lines 1042-1048).
Conclude from well-foundedness that B has no element at all, which closes the first direction (source lines 1049).

Assume every nonempty subset merely has a minimal element, take the subset of elements that are not accessible, and use the hypothesis on it to obtain an element that is merely accessible (source lines 1051-1054).

Apply excluded middle and induction on truncation to turn mere accessibility into accessibility, contradicting membership in that subset, so the subset is empty and the relation is well-founded (source lines 1055-1056).

proof_roadmap.step: First direction: no-minimal-element subset is empty, by induction on accessibility.
Second direction: apply the hypothesis to the subset of non-accessible elements.
Excluded middle plus induction on truncation gives the contradiction.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 1037-1040: under excluded middle, a relation is well-founded exactly when every nonempty subset merely has a minimal element. The proof (source lines 1041-1057) is carried out in full in both directions and its substance is not visible in the statement: the first direction introduces an auxiliary claim that no accessible element lies in a subset with no minimal element and establishes it by induction on the accessibility witness, using the merely existing smaller element together with access to the induction hypothesis at that element; the second direction forms the subset of non-accessible elements, applies the minimal-element hypothesis to it, and closes the argument by excluded middle together with induction on truncation, which is the step that turns mere accessibility into accessibility. Two directions, an auxiliary induction and a truncation induction are the substance of the card.
